title: Autophagy modulates glioblastoma cell sensitivity to Selinexor-mediated XPO1 inhibition.
authors: Tang, Yongjian; Sprinzen, Lisa; Terada, Yukinori; Kiang, Karrie M; Li, Chuntao; Zeng, Yu; Liu, Fangkun; Zhou, Hongshu; Liang, Xisong; Zhang, Jianzhong; Pieper, Russell O; Chen, Bo; Zhang, Liyang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Selinexor在胶质母细胞瘤中诱导自噬的机制，涉及XPO1抑制和TFEB核滞留，但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Selinexor is a selective inhibitor of exportin-1 (XPO1), a key mediator of the nucleocytoplasmic transport for molecules critical to tumor cell survival. Selinexor's lethality is generally associated with the induction of apoptosis, and in some cases, with autophagy-induced apoptosis. We performed this study to determine Selinexor's action in glioblastoma (GBM) cells, which are notoriously resistant to apoptosis. METHODS: Patient-derived GBM cells were treated with Selinexor, and drug response and autophagy levels were monitored. Homozygous C528S XPO1 mutant GBM43 cells were generated by CRISPR/Cas9 editing. Single Selinexor or combination treatment with autophagy inhibitors was evaluated. In addition, bulk-tissue, single-cell, and spatial transcriptome were analyzed, and molecular docking was performed. RESULTS: Although all cell lines exhibited a dose- and time-dependent reduction of cell viability, the most profound molecular response to Selinexor was induction of autophagy instead of apoptosis. Selinexor-induced autophagy was an on-target consequence of XPO1 inhibition, and could be mitigated by expression of a mutant, Selinexor-resistant form of XPO1, and Selinexor-induced autophagy was related at least in part to nuclear trapping of the transcription factor TFEB. Furthermore, genetic or pharmacologic suppression of autophagy sensitized the cells to Selinexor-induced toxicity in association with the induction of apoptosis. Finally, in intracranial PDX studies, the combination of Selinexor with the autophagy inhibitor chloroquine significantly impeded tumor growth and extended mouse survival relative to single-agent treatment. CONCLUSION: These results suggest that activation of autophagy confers a protective mechanism against Selinexor in GBM cells, and that the combination of Selinexor with autophagy inhibitors may serve as a viable means to enhance Selinexor-induced cell death.
abstract_zh: 背景：Selinexor是一种选择性exportin-1（XPO1）抑制剂，XPO1是肿瘤细胞存活关键分子核质转运的重要介导因子。Selinexor的致死作用通常与凋亡诱导相关，在某些情况下也与自噬诱导的凋亡有关。我们开展本研究以确定Selinexor在胶质母细胞瘤（glioblastoma, GBM）细胞中的作用，这些细胞以对凋亡具有显著抵抗性而著称。方法：使用患者来源的GBM细胞处理Selinexor，监测药物反应和自噬水平。通过CRISPR/Cas9编辑生成纯合C528S XPO1突变体GBM43细胞。评估单药Selinexor或与自噬抑制剂联合治疗的效果。此外，分析了组织块、单细胞和空间转录组，并进行了分子对接。结果：尽管所有细胞系均表现出剂量和时间依赖性的细胞活力降低，但Selinexor最显著的分子反应是诱导自噬而非凋亡。Selinexor诱导的自噬是XPO1抑制的靶向后果，可通过表达突变型、Selinexor抗性形式的XPO1来缓解，且Selinexor诱导的自噬至少部分与转录因子TFEB的核滞留相关。此外，遗传或药理学抑制自噬使细胞对Selinexor诱导的毒性敏感化，并伴随凋亡的诱导。最后，在颅内PDX研究中，与单药治疗相比，Selinexor与自噬抑制剂氯喹的联合使用显著抑制了肿瘤生长并延长了小鼠生存期。结论：这些结果表明，自噬的激活赋予GBM细胞对Selinexor的保护机制，而Selinexor与自噬抑制剂的联合使用可能作为增强Selinexor诱导细胞死亡的有效手段。
